title: AI & Quantum Chemistry Boost Blue OLED Efficiency Beyond 25% Limit
summary: Researchers at Nagoya University and Kyushu University combined quantum chemistry and machine learning to design boron-free thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) molecules. From a virtual library of over 19,000 candidates they synthesized two blue emitters with 93–99% photoluminescence yield; devices reached near-Rec.2020 color and a maximum external quantum efficiency of 35.2%, surpassing the conventional 25% blue OLED limit.
content:
Researchers at the Institute of Transformative Bio-Molecules at Nagoya University and the Institute for Advanced Study at Kyushu University are addressing a longstanding challenge in display technology: the inefficiency of blue OLED pixels. Conventional fluorescent blue OLEDs are limited to 25% efficiency, a stark contrast to the nearly 100% internal quantum efficiency achieved by red and green pixels using heavy-metal-based emitters. This disparity arises because blue light demands higher excited-state energy, which accelerates degradation in iridium-based blue emitters and has prompted a search for alternative organic solutions.

The research team combined quantum chemistry methods with machine learning to identify new organic molecules for thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) without relying on boron frameworks. Recognizing that boron-containing designs are often synthetically complex, they systematically explored boron-free 13-ring structures built from linked five- and six-membered rings. The effort generated a virtual library of more than 19,000 candidate molecules that were screened computationally for the electronic properties needed for efficient blue TADF.

From that computational screening, the researchers synthesized two promising compounds that exhibited vivid blue emission with narrow spectral bandwidths and exceptionally high photoluminescence quantum yields of 93–99% in thin films, indicating highly efficient light emission. One device based on a molecule labeled Cz-PAH-1 approached the blue-primary color coordinates required by the Rec.2020 ultra-high-definition display standard, while a device using Cz-PAH-2 achieved a maximum external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 35.2%, significantly exceeding the conventional 25% limit for fluorescent blue pixels.

The work, published in Angewandte Chemie International Edition on July 21, 2026, demonstrates a streamlined integrated workflow that couples quantum-chemical simulation and artificial intelligence to accelerate the discovery of functional organic materials. The researchers emphasize that the same combined approach could speed development of other organic optoelectronic materials beyond OLED applications, reducing reliance on synthetically challenging elements and heavy metals.

Source: https://www.itbm.nagoya-u.ac.jp/en/research/2026/07/post-120.php
